en: The Scripture on the Divine Incantation Praising the Merits of the Tathāgata, in one fascicle,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing under Imperial Commission during the Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Bhagavān was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha,
together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus.
There were twelve thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas present together,
all of whom were great bodhisattvas of the Bhadrakalpa.
At that time, the World-Honored One was among this assembly.
He addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, saying:
"If there are good sons or good daughters who [hear] the names of the supreme, wondrous, and auspicious Tathāgatas currently residing in the ten directions..."
If one recollects, upholds, and single-mindedly reveres the name of this Tathāgata,
all karmic obstructions, retributive obstructions, and grave offenses of broken precepts will be entirely extinguished.
The supreme, wondrous, and virtuous roots of goodness,
genuine merits, and all virtues— including exhortations, sympathetic joy, dedication, and the making of vows—
constitute the bodhicitta that never regresses.

I now wish to speak; you should listen attentively. Homage to the Tathāgata Vimalaprabha of the eastern direction. Homage to the Tathāgata Gaṇavicitrasaṃbhava of the southeastern direction. Homage to the Tathāgata Vimalacandradhvajapatirāja of the southern direction. Homage to the Tathāgata Arciṣmativicitra of the southwestern direction. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnavijaya of the western direction. Homage to the Tathāgata Kumāraprabha of the northwestern direction. Homage to the Tathāgata Abhayavimalaghoṣa of the northern direction. Homage to the Tathāgata Mahāyaśas-vigatabhaya-saṃtrāsa of the northeastern direction. Homage to the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrāntagāmin of the upper direction. Homage to the Tathāgata Suvarṇapuṣpaprabha of the lower direction. At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva Maitreya.
To the east, passing from here through ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddha-lands as numerous as motes of dust,
there is a Buddha-world named Wondrous Pearl.
In that land there is a Buddha.

He is titled the Tathāgata Rightly and Universally Knowing, the Supreme Jewel King, Unstained, Exalted Above the Dharma Realm, Adorned by Vast Transformations, Adorned by the Power of Vows, and Adorned by the Radiance of Boundless Suns and Moons; his crown protuberance (*uṣṇīṣa*) possesses wondrous marks, and his body is of the color of lapis lazuli, with the lotus-flame of stainless light and the merit of the eye of space, adorned with the most sublime fragrance and offerings of various exquisite colors.
He bestowed the prediction of enlightenment upon the bodhisattva Anupama.

Following the parinirvāṇa of that Buddha, he shall attain Buddhahood, known by the name Lakṣaṇavicitra-sūryapradīpa-candraprabha-padma-kanakavarṇa-gaganapūrṇa-vipula-prabhāsa-samanta-vyūha-maṇḍala-daśadik-sarva-loka-vyakti-ketu-rāja-samyaksambuddha Tathāgata. His body color will be like gold, filling the realm of space; his light will be vast, unimpeded, and adorned with a halo that universally illuminates the ten directions, such that there is nothing it does not clearly manifest. He shall be a sovereign king of banners and standards, a Truly All-Knowing Tathāgata.
The Buddha said, "Maitreya,
you should know that if there are sons or daughters of good family who are able to receive,
uphold, prostrate to, and single-mindedly revere the names of these Buddhas,"
During these ten days, one should personally confess one's transgressions. Furthermore,
by means of the supreme and wondrous roots of goodness arising from exhortation, sympathetic joy, dedication, and making vows, all karmic obstructions,
retributive obstructions, violations of the precepts, and grave offenses shall be completely extinguished.
Although dwelling within birth and death, they are not exempt from the cycle of transmigration;
yet they never fall away from their aspiration for bodhicitta.
In whatever place they are born, they will be of noble and distinguished lineage.
They will remain far removed from poverty, lowly status, and inferior birth;
their six sense faculties will be complete, they will be loved and respected by all, and their appearance will be peerlessly handsome.
They will always encounter virtuous friends and never meet with evil persons.
All their aspirations and requests shall be fulfilled according to their wishes;
there shall be nothing regarding wealth, treasures, or honorable positions that does not accord with their hearts' desires.
After the end of their lives, they shall be reborn in the lands of the various Buddhas.
Having first performed such rites of prostration and repentance,
one should recite this dhāraṇī with a sincere mind. Then,
the mantra is spoken as follows:
Tadyathā: akṣe mokṣe samantamukhe svāhīyute.
Dhani samayogī cittavibhāta.
A-khye-mu-khye-sa-ta-da-ni-bi-be-de.
Samantakṣaṇasattvalokamudritapramuditahele mule musale.
Asmṛti smṛty-ajite mṛtyu-jite!
bodhicittam utpādayāmi.
Sindibhaṅge 'moghavati svasti svasti.
Dharma-chen-te-a-be-si-pi-ho-lo-di-pi.
*Saitendā-vi-bhāti svāhā*.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke in verse:
Six billion great ṛṣis all receive and uphold this dhāraṇī;
constantly mindful and undistracted, wherever they dwell throughout the ten directions in their present lives,
they always encounter virtuous spiritual friends.
All those who have aspirations, by recollecting this,
shall see all the Buddhas appear before them according to their wishes;
those who constantly hold this mantra while seated upon a lotus throne will be born through transformation, endowed with the auspicious marks.
Mindfulness and concentration are both secure and peaceful; wisdom increases and becomes ever more luminous.
One is able to receive and uphold what is heard, never forgetting the meaning of the various phrases.
If one upholds the names of all Buddhas, this becomes a place of refuge for the world.
They shall not fall into the evil realms, but will always be born within the good destinies;
by the power of the Buddha, these people shall always attain superior states until they realize enlightenment, as they constantly cultivate sublime conduct.
If one were to take Buddha-lands numbering many billions, filled with gold, and offer them as a gift;
the mass of merit of a person who upholds the name of the Buddha would exceed that.
Such a person is worthy of offerings and will be reborn wherever they may go.
Born into a family of eternal wealth and nobility, they are courageous and bold, practicing giving without stinginess.
From their mouths there constantly issues every kind of fragrance, including the celestial red sandalwood scent, for many hundreds of billions of kalpas.
If a person writes down the names of the Buddhas within their home and makes offerings to them,
their family and retinue will always be peaceful and secure, free from all afflictions and disturbances.
If a person constantly recites and upholds them, they shall enjoy long life and freedom from illness.
May one always encounter virtuous friends, and at the time of death, remain undisturbed in mind.
This mass of the Tathāgata’s merit is inconceivable in its measure;
the wise should recite and uphold it, practicing with diligence and never being heedless.
At that time, the Bhagavat,
having spoken this sutra for the sake of Maitreya Bodhisattva and the great assembly,
[entered into meditative absorption].
The Bodhisattva Maitreya and the others, along with the great assembly of bhikṣus, humans, and devas,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
were all greatly rejoiced; they received it upon their heads and practiced accordingly.
The Scripture on the Divine Incantation Praising the Merits of the Tathāgata, Spoken by the Buddha, in one fascicle.
